items.title: Tell HN: Firefox's default browser check dark pattern triggers Windows BSOD
items.excerpt: Been pulling my hair out debugging a relative’s persistent BSOD (once every ~6hrs) after nudging them to take the first degoogling step by switching browsers. I could not believe at first that a user space program, especially a Windows Store sandboxed one, could affect anything in the kernel, but analyzing every single coredump shows the exact same trigger: Firefox attempted to rename the UrlAssocistions/http registry key in the UWP sandbox’s virtualized registry hive, triggering an access violation in the Registry system service and crashing ntoskrnl. items.title: Capitalism Can't Handle AI
items.excerpt: Capitalism as a system of profit-seeking agents can't handle AI right. There is a very simple feedback loop: 1. Agents seek to increase their profit by automating people. 2. Each agent acts to its own good but at the same moment, the ultimate goal is to get rid of all consumers of what agents produce, because jobless people are very bad at consuming goods and services. 3. Agents don't have any motivation to provide goods and services to consumers if they don't get anything valuable in return. Conclusion is simple. Either: a. AI development will be completely regulated and jobs will be preserved (thus negating the promised AI effectiveness), or b. Capitalism will be destroyed and a completely new economical formation will take place. It is AI or capitalism.

items.title: Sales calculation tool for Excel price lists
items.excerpt: Hi HN, I built a sales calculation tool for teams that still rely heavily on Excel for product pricing and quote calculations. The idea is to keep the useful part of Excel instead of forcing sales teams to rebuild all of their pricing logic somewhere else. A salesperson can upload an Excel file (which is saved in IndexedDB locally on the persons computer), create a customer-specific calculation from it and generate offer PDFs or order confirmation PDFs. The calculation can also be connected to customer data, contacts, products and machines in a database so the salesperson does not have to keep copying the same information. I started working on this because there seem to be a lot of B2B sales processes where the actual pricing logic still lives in spreadsheets. items.title: Ask HN: Where has creativity in software gone?
items.excerpt: I sometimes read Show HN, and there is literally no creativity at all: note-taker app after note-taker clone. Everyone is essentially looking at what’s already there, and they say, “Why can’t I create the exact same product, but worse, and add an AI suffix?” There is nothing creative about AI. Show HN might as well be renamed “Prompt HN.” These promoters always say, “Prompting makes me efficient; I don’t have to write code by hand anymore.” Great. What has your “efficiency” gotten you? Yet another note-taker with an “AI” suffix? I could take notes in 1990. Where did the actual engineers go? Surely they aren’t all selling ads at Facebook’s spyware empire? Where are the transistor, the C programming language, Emacs, and SQLite developers of our time?

items.title: Ask HN: How do you decide an idea is worth building before you start coding?
items.excerpt: I’ve been thinking about the gap between having an idea and actually deciding it deserves weeks or months of work. Building has become much cheaper. A developer can prototype something surprisingly fast now. But the decision before building still seems messy. When you’re evaluating an idea, what evidence do you actually trust? Customer interviews? Existing workarounds? Competitor reviews? Search demand? People already paying for alternatives? Your own experience with the problem? And maybe more importantly: What evidence would make you decide not to build it? I often see founders collect a lot of information, but the final decision still comes down to a mix of browser tabs, notes, spreadsheets and gut feeling. Curious how HN founders and developers actually make this decision in practice. Have you found a process that works consistently?
